review_comments.body:
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Keep review state outside the readable workspace**

When the semantic projection runs without an explicit `CHAT_PROCEDURE_STATE_ROOT` and without `LOCALAPPDATA`, `controlPlaneEnvironment` places procedure state under `CHAT_LOCAL_FILES_ROOT/.chat-agent-platform/procedure-state`. Registering this launch variant lets the development caller create the genesis there, and the returned `operation_key` identifies its filename; the existing `workspace_read` tool can then read that file and extract the supposedly private `review_run_id`. Once dispatch is opened— including after upgrading this persisted operation to the later automation slice—the caller can use that capability to submit a forged automatic result. Store review state outside the workspace-readable root or explicitly deny workspace access to the state directory.

review_comments.body:
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Include review modules in the installed runtime bundle**

On a clean Windows bootstrap, `Install-ChatManagerBundle` copies this updated `cli.py`, but its `$runtimeFiles` list in `scripts/bootstrap-manager-runtime.ps1` omits both `independent_review_procedures.py` and `independent_review_state.py` (and the later Windows procedure installer does not supply them either). Consequently the installed CLI raises `ModuleNotFoundError` at this import before the semantic inventory preflight can start, breaking the normal six-tool runtime. The workflow's standalone-layout test manually copies these files, so it does not exercise the production installer omission. Add both modules to the installed bundle and its required/provenance checks.

review_comments.body:
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject parent roots that place review state in the workspace**

When `CHAT_PROCEDURE_STATE_ROOT` is the parent of the readable workspace and that workspace is `<state_root>/independent-review-v1`, this one-way `relative_to` check passes even though `_review_root()` writes the genesis directly into the workspace. Fresh evidence beyond the earlier comment is that this inverse layout still lets `launch_independent_review_v1` create a readable genesis, while the returned `operation_key` identifies its filename; `workspace_read` can therefore recover `review_run_id` and use it to forge submission once that persisted operation reaches `dispatch-attempted`. Check the actual review-state directory for overlap in both directions, rather than only rejecting state roots beneath the workspace.

However, `scripts/prepare-windows-case-l3.ps1` omits both files from `$criticalAssets` (lines 75-102) and `$installedMappings` (lines 130-144), and the final provenance recheck hashes only those recorded mappings. review_comments.body:
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Guard the configured review-state root for the whole session**

When `CHAT_PROCEDURE_STATE_ROOT` names a custom directory outside `${platformRoot}/state`, this launcher checks only the default manager-state tree. Fresh evidence beyond the earlier state-overlap comment is that, after an operation was created with a safe workspace, the profile can be restarted with that custom state directory as `CHAT_LOCAL_FILES_ROOT`; startup succeeds and `workspace_read` can read the existing genesis and private `review_run_id` before the CLI's per-procedure overlap guard runs. Derive and reject overlap with the actual configured `independent-review-v1` directory during launcher startup.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L167-L172](https://github.com/BogdanAIP/chat-agent-platform/blob/8c6ae17d6588b98813e97fe143f11d0bef249a81/AGENTS.md#L167-L172)

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

CONFIRMED. Fixed on current head `858dcb7dd065717ea0d59b1e7b931b13a844f8d4`. The canonical semantic launcher now derives the actual configured `CHAT_PROCEDURE_STATE_ROOT/independent-review-v1` boundary at startup and rejects workspace overlap in either direction before inventory or any semantic child starts. It resolves physical paths and, for not-yet-created state, resolves the nearest existing physical ancestor so a future private state placement inside the current workspace is rejected before creation. The regression covers persisted custom state, parent/child layouts, future not-yet-created state, and junction/symlink aliases. I also applied the same configured-review-root boundary to legacy `files-readonly`/`adaptive` profile startup so profile switching cannot expose a persisted custom reviewer capability. Exact-head CI is pending; no final PASS is claimed yet.
